key_insight: A physics-assisted deep neural network can close the unclosed thermodynamic-gradient effects in compressible velocity-gradient dynamics by combining phenomenological and data-driven models for pressure-Hessian, baroclinic, and vibrational non-equilibrium contributions.
engineering_relevance: The H-EHEE framework offers a more accurate surrogate for predicting small-scale flow evolution in highly compressible regimes, which is useful for CFD modeling of high-speed aerothermodynamics.
method: Uses a hybrid closure for the thermodynamic gradient field tensor in velocity-gradient equations.
Learns the inviscid baroclinic tensor mechanism with a neural network and a novel non-symmetric tensor basis.
Adds data-driven closure terms for vibrational non-equilibrium alongside existing phenomenological pressure-Hessian models.
evidence_signal: The model is evaluated across multiple turbulent Mach numbers and shows close agreement with DNS statistics, outperforming existing compressible velocity-gradient models, especially at high compressibility.
watch_item: Performance depends on the training data regime and the validity of the learned tensor closures when extrapolating to flow conditions outside the simulated Mach-number range.
paper_title: A physics-assisted deep neural network-based closure framework for velocity gradient dynamics in compressible flows with vibrational non-equilibrium
